sentences.text: JUDGMENT
Suit is one for permanent injunction to restrain the defendant from interfering with the plaintiff's possession and enjoyment over the schedule property.

2. Case of the plaintiff in brief is as here under:-
One Sri. Venkataramanappa was the absolute owner of 20 guntas land situated in Sy.
No.29/5 of Giddakonenahalli Village, Yeshwanthapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk having acquired the same under registered Sale Deed dated 14.06.1954 executed by its erstwhile owner Mr. Thimmanna S/o. Maraiah.
The said Venkataramanappa passed away on 07.07.1986.
During his life time, 20 guntas of land in Sy. No.95/5 was given to the plaintiff who was his daughter.

After the death of Venkataramanappa, the brothers of the plaintiff by name Venkatarangaiah, Venkatahanumaiah, Lakshmi Narayana and mother of the plaintiff namely Chikka Hanumakka submitted no objection to effect khata in her name.
Accordingly, khata is transferred to the name of plaintiff and she is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property as absolute owner thereof since more than 4 decades.

It is stated that as per M.R. No.66/2003-04 dated 11.06.2004 the old Sy. No.29/5 was renumbered as Sy. No.51 and the RTCs shows that the plaintiff is in possession and enjoyment of 20 guntas of land in Sy. No.51.
3.

Later, the defendant B.D.A. issued a preliminary notification dated 04.09.2003 for acquisition of 4 acres of land in Sy. No.51 of Giddakonenahalli Village for the purpose of further extension of Sir.
M.Vishweshwaraiah Nagar.
Later it acquired only 3 acres of land in Sy. No.51 as per the copy of the award dated 29.11.2003 passed under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act.
It is stated that the remaining extent of 1 acre out of 4 acres was, left out from acquisition in Sy. No.51 and it was restored to the owners.
Thus the plaintiff was restored with possession of 20 guntas of land which is comprised in 1 acre of land, left out from acquisition.

The said 1 acre of the land now comes with the Varalakshmamma vs Bangalore Development Authority on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26917125/
2 jurisdiction of B.B.M.P.
Thus, the plaintiff being the owner of 20 guntas of land in Sy. No.51 is in possession and enjoyment of the same.

Such being the factual position, the defendant B.D.A. having no manner of right, title or interest interfered with the possession of the plaintiff on 07.03.2014 and made attempts to dig and make marking on the schedule property which was resisted by the plaintiff.

It is the apprehension of the plaintiff that the defendant may at any point of time dispossess the plaintiff from the suit schedule property and hence, the cause of action to file the suit arose and hence, the suit.
4. In pursuance to the summons issued the defendant caused appearance and filed written statement, wherein which it has categorically denied the averments made in the plaint.

However,
there is an admission that the B.D.A. had issued preliminary notification dated 04.09.2003 for acquisition of 4 acres of land in Sy. No.51 of Giddakonenahalli village for further extension of Sir.
M.Vishweswaraiah Nagar and out of the total extent, only 3 acres of the land was required and hence it acquired only 3 acres of land in Sy. No.51 and it is admitted that 1 acre of land was left out of acquisition in Sy. No.51.

But the defendant B.D.A. has pleaded ignorance about the possession and enjoyment of the plaintiff over the 20 guntas of land and as to the payment of tax to the B.B.M.P.
and has denied the cause of action to file the suit.

It is stated that out of the total extent of 4 acres in Sy. No.51, 3 acres of land was acquired vide preliminary notification dated 08.04.2003 and final notification dated 09.09.2003 and award was passed and approved on 19.11.2003 and possession of 3 acres of land was taken on 05.12.2003 and the compensation amount is deposited before the Principal City Civil Judge, Bengaluru dated 24.11.2003.

Hence there is no cause of action to file the suit and the alleged cause of action is imaginary and the plaintiff is not entitled for any relief and sought for dismissal of suit.
5. Heard learned counsel for plaintiff and defendant.
6. The aforesaid pleadings have occasioned following:-
ISSUES 1.
Whether the plaintiff proves that she is in possession of the schedule property ?
2. Whether the plaintiff further proves alleged interference of the defendant with her possession of the schedule property ?
3. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the relief sought for ?
4. What Order of Decree?

8.

Before adverting to the merits of the case it is considered to worth to take note of the undisputed facts, which is apparent from the evidence and pleadings placed on record.
It is an undisputed fact that B.D.A. had notified for acquisition of 4 acres of land in Sy. No.51 of Giddakonenahalli Village for the purpose of further extension of Sir. M.Vishweshwaraiah Nagar.

Later it acquired 3 acres of land for the purpose of formation of further extension of Sir M.Visweswaraiah Nagar in preliminary notification No.BDA/Commr/SLAO/ 2003-04 dated 08.04.2003, duly published in the Karnataka Gazette dated 09.04.2003 and final notification No.UDD/749/MNX/2003 dated 09.09.2003 in published in the Karnataka Gazette dated 10.09.2003 and award passed and approved on 19.11.2003 and possession of the land is taken on 05.12.2003 and the compensation is deposited before the couirt vide BR. It also an undisputed fact that the remaining 1 acre of land in Sy. No.51 was dropped from acquisition.

After the death of Venkataramanappa, the brothers of the plaintiff by name Venkatarangaiah, Venkatahanumaiah, Lakshmi Narayana and mother of the plaintiff namely Chikka Hanumakka submitted no objection to effect khata in her name.
Accordingly, khata is transferred to the name of plaintiff and she is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property as absolute owner owner thereof since more than 4 decades.

It is stated that as per M.R.

In order to substantiate the same, P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P.2 to Ex.P.5 which are the RTCs and mutation extract which shows that RTC from the year 1986-87 in respect of the land bearing Sy.
No.29/5 measuring 4 acres stood in the name of Thammanna and it shows the name of plaintiff is mutated to an extent of 20 guntas by virtue of IHC-1/87-88.
So the revenue records shows, by virtue of inheritance, 20 guntas of land is mutated to the name of plaintiff.

So far as the renumbering of old Sy. No.29/5 as Sy. No.51 is concerned, the mutation extract Ex.P.5, clearly shows that the property bearing Sy. No.29/5 measuring 20 guntas which stood in the name of the plaintiff is renumbered as Sy. No.51 along with other properties by virtue of the order passed by the Tahsildar and accordingly, mutation is accepted to the name of plaintiff in respect of Sy. No.51.
15.
Ex.P.6 is the RTC which shows Sy. No.51 to an extent of 20 guntas stood in the name of Varalakshmamma.

Subsequently, the property came within the limits of B.B.M.P. and Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.4 shows the plaintiff is paying tax to B.B.M.P.
16.

P.W.1 has further deposed that the defendant B.D.A. issued a preliminary notification dated 04.09.2003 for acquisition of 4 acres of land in Sy. No.51 of Giddakonenahalli Village for the purpose of further extension of Sir. M.Vishweshwaraiah Nagar.
Later it acquired only 3 acres of land in Sy. No.51 as per the copy of the award dated 29.11.2003 passed under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act.
It is stated that the remaining extent of 1 acre, out of 4 acres was left out from acquisition in Sy. No.51 and it was restored to the owners.
Thus the plaintiff was restored with possession of 20 guntas of land which is comprised in 1 acre of land left out from acquisition.
The said 1 acre of the land now comes with the jurisdiction of B.B.M.P.

sentences.text: As stated earlier, it is specific defense of the defendant that there was no interference on the part of the defendant and they have only proceeded with the marking of the acquired property and not in respect of the property which is left out and hence, there is no question of B.D.A. interfering with the unacquired land which belongs to the plaintiff.
During cross-examination of P.W.1 he admits the officials of B.D.A. have not caused any kind of interference, but he says attempts were made to encroach his property.
There is an admission that out of 4 acres, possession of 3 acres was taken by B.D.A. and 1 acre was restored to the owners and P.W.1 says 20 guntas belonged to the plaintiff.

So far as the interference is concerned, P.W.1 says, the defendants made attempts to take possession and he says the suit was filed before the 1 acre of land was left out from acquisition and the suggestion putforth that a false suit is filed against the B.D.A. is denied.

18. So from the oral evidence of P.W.1 and the documents relied upon by him it is evident that the plaintiff has succeeded in proving her possession over the suit schedule property, but there is a clear admission that there is no interference on the part of B.D.A. and it is also admitted that the suit was filed before the 1 acre of land was left out from acquisition.
So though the evidence of P.W.1 and the documents relied upon by him proves the possession of plaintiff over suit property, his evidence do not prove the interference caused by the defendant.

19. On the contrary, the defendant got examined through its Superintendent LAO Section B.D.A. as D.W.1 and he has in his evidence deposed that the suit for permanent injunction as against the defendant is not maintainable and it is stated that the B.D.A. issued preliminary notification No.
BDA/Commr/ SLAO/2003-04 dated 08.04.2003, duly published in the Karnataka Gazette dated 09.04.2003 and final notification No. UDD/749/MNX/2003 dated 09.09.2003 published in the Karnataka Gazette dated 10.09.2003 and award passed and approved on 19.11.2003 and possession of the land is taken on 05.12.2003 and the compensation is deposited before the court in BR.
No.104/22.11.2013 vide Cheque No.635916 dated 24.11.2003 and thus there is no cause of action to file the suit and sought for dismissal of suit.

20. D.W.1 has produced Ex.D.2 to Ex.D.6 which are the preliminary notification dated 09.04.2003 and final notification dated 10.09.2003 and the award passed by LAO and mahazar for taking possession of the suit schedule property and the notification for taking possession and all these documents shows the B.D.A. has issued preliminary notification for acquisition of Sy. No.51 along with other properties for the purpose of formation of Sir. M.Visweswaraiahnagar and the khathedars are shown as Venkataramanappa and his wife and children as khatedars and which shows 4 acres of land is proposed for acquisition.
However, Ex.D.3 final notification shows out of the total extent of 4 acres in Sy.No.51, 3 acres is acquired for acquisition and 1 acre land is left out.

Accordingly, as per Ex.D.4 award is passed only to an extent of 3 acres and possession of property is taken only to an extent of 3 acres of land in Sy. No.51 as per Ex.D.5 and possession notification is also issued as per to an extent of 3 acres in Sy. No.51 and this is also accompanied by the sketch.

Ex.D.6 is the notification under Section 16(2) of Land Acquisition Act which shows possession of 3 acres of land is Varalakshmamma vs Bangalore Development Authority on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26917125/
6 taken in Sy. No.51.

sentences.text: The sketch placed on record also corroborates the said defense raised by defendants.
As stated earlier, it has remained undisputed that 1 acre of land was restored to the owner and it was not acquired for compensation.

21. During cross-examination of D.W.1 there is a clear admission that the suit schedule property measuring 20 guntas is not acquired by the defendant and no award is passed and compensation is not issued to the khathedars.

So this admission of D.W.2 establishes the possession of plaintiff over the suit schedule property, but nothing is elicited in the cross of D.W.1 to prove the interference caused by B.D.A.
22.

Further, the defendant has examined the Assistant Executive Engineer of B.D.A. as D.W.2 and he has in his evidence deposed that the plaintiff has raised question that the defendant encroached the non- acquired property of the plaintiff, but the defendant formed the layout in 3 acres, sites were formed only in 3 acres of land and no attempts were made to encroach the schedule property.
D.W.2 has produced Ex.D.7 which is approved layout plan in Sy. No.51.
During his cross-examination he says he has no knowledge about the suit schedule property apart from the acquired property.
23. On analysis of the oral and documentary evidence relied upon by both the parties, it is evident that, as stated earlier, acquisition of 3 acres of land in Sy. No.51 has remained undisputed.
Further the documents relied upon by the plaintiff and also the admission of D.W.1 in his cross-examination establishes the possession and enjoyment of the plaintiff over the 20 guntas of land.

24. It is necessary to note that in a suit for permanent injunction the burden is upon the plaintiff to not only establish possession, but it is equally obligatory on the plaintiff to establish the interference caused by the defendant.

Apart from contending that the defendant made attempts to interfere with the possession, there is nothing forthcoming to show that she has filed representation before the B.D.A. about the attempts made to encroach the property or as to any complaint before jurisdictional police.

Added to this, the admission of P.W.1 in her cross-examination that no interference was caused by the B.D.A. itself makes it clear that there was no interference on the part of defendant in respect of suit schedule property.

The evidence of D.W.1 and 2 shows that they are not asserting any right over the unacquired property and they have only formed layout in 3 acres of land in Sy. No.51 and have not made any attempts to encroach upon the unacquired land.

So in view of admission of P.W.1 in his cross-examination coupled with the evidence of D.W.1 and 2, this Court is of opinion that though the plaintiff has succeeded in establishing her possession over the suit property, she has failed to prove the interference caused by the defendant and hence, the plaintiff is not entitled for the relief claimed.
Accordingly, this Court proceeds to answer the aforesaid issue No.1 in the Affirmative and issues No.2 and 3 in the Negative.
25. ISSUE NO.4 ::

In view of findings given on Issues No.1 to 3, this Court proceeds to pass the following;
ORDER Suit of the plaintiff is dismissed.
Plaintiff shall bear the cost of the suit.
Draw decree accordingly.
